clues: This small town sits on a river where the tide runs out. Past this point, the sea no longer lifts the stream.
Winters here are cold, windy, and full of snow. On most nights in mid winter, the air sinks to ten degrees or less.
In 1827, this river town won the capital job. It beat out three rival towns that wanted the honor, including the state's big port city.
Of all the state capitals in the land, this one sits farthest east. It is the first to catch the sun each day.
The governor of Maine works in this small city. State lawmakers meet here, beside the river.
